audit_findings.title: China sanctions could create a discontinuity absent from the scenarios
audit_findings.magnitude: approximately $537.0 million of revenue and $142.0 million of adjusted EBIT exposure, computed from the filed 6% and 20% shares; inventory, receivable and relocation losses unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Potential sanctions could abruptly reduce OE, require working-capital write-offs and impair the growth path rather than producing the scenarios' gradual decline.
audit_findings.evidence: Approximately 6 % and 20% of our revenue and income before interest and taxes (excluding goodwill and other intangible asset impairment charges recorded in 2025), respectively, were generated in China in each of 2024 and 2025.
audit_findings.explanation: This is a consequential unresolved possibility, not a demonstrated valuation error: PVH was on the UEL, but no measures had been imposed as of August 2, 2026. The exposed adjusted EBIT is about 35.6% of the $398.7 million OE anchor, so implementation of broad restrictions could change the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Run a discrete China shutdown and restricted-sourcing case using China operating earnings, inventory, receivables and relocation costs; update the status immediately if MOFCOM imposes measures.

audit_findings.title: The FY2025 anchor predates a known 2026 tariff step-up
audit_findings.magnitude: $195 million gross 2026 exposure, equal to 48.9% of the $398.7 million anchor; mitigation is unquantified; the separate realized tariff-refund benefit was $106.7 million
audit_findings.mechanism: The post-anchor recurring tariff burden enters first-year OE through cost of goods sold, while the tariff refund is a nonrecurring benefit that should not support continuing growth.
audit_findings.evidence: We currently expect an estimated net negative impact on our full year 2026 gross profit, including a gross impact of approximately $195 million and a partially offsetting impact from planned mitigation actions.
audit_findings.explanation: The anchor is a valid historical actual, but projecting 2% growth from it without a post-tariff reconciliation is a demonstrated forecast gap. The filed gross exposure is large enough to change the conclusion, although the continuing net effect remains unknown because mitigation was not quantified and trade policy changed during 2026.
audit_findings.action: Rebuild first-year OE from the 2026 year-to-date results, separately identify recurring tariff costs, realized mitigation and the $106.7 million refund, and rerun every scenario from post-tariff recurring OE.

audit_findings.title: The null perimeter misses an active license-to-wholesale conversion
audit_findings.magnitude: filed 2026 effect of less than 1% additional revenue and approximately 50 basis points lower gross margin; 50 basis points on $8.950 billion of 2025 revenue is approximately $44.8 million, or 11.2% of the OE anchor, before offsets
audit_findings.mechanism: The conversion replaces royalty income with wholesale revenue, inventory, working capital, operating expenses and capital requirements, affecting both OE and reinvestment.
audit_findings.evidence: We have been directly operating a significant portion of the businesses for the Calvin Klein and TOMMY HILFIGER product categories previously licensed to G-III in the United States and Canada, and we intend to continue to directly operate a significant portion of these businesses as the license agreements expire, through 2026, with the remainder being re-licensed to other third parties.
audit_findings.explanation: The null perimeter is demonstrably incomplete because the conversion is active and has filed revenue and margin effects. Its net value direction and materiality remain unresolved: revenue increases, gross margin declines, and the filing does not isolate incremental OE or working-capital investment.
audit_findings.action: Create a perimeter schedule separating converted categories from the legacy business and rerun OE using their incremental revenue, gross profit, operating costs, inventory, receivables, payables, capital expenditure and transition costs.

audit_findings.title: The bridge may add non-excess foreign cash at full value
audit_findings.magnitude: $427 million of foreign cash, equal to $8.83 per share and 6.8% of base equity value; even removing the entire $965.9 million cash balance would reduce base value by $19.96 per share and the 30%-MOS buy-below level to approximately $76.69 versus the $74.33 price
audit_findings.mechanism: Operationally required, restricted or tax-burdened cash should reduce the cash added in the equity bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: Our intent is to reinvest indefinitely substantially all of our historical earnings in foreign subsidiaries outside of the United States in jurisdictions which we would expect to incur material tax costs upon the distribution of such amounts.
audit_findings.explanation: The full-value treatment is not proven correct, and $427 million was held internationally with potentially material distribution taxes. Nevertheless, the concrete outer bound—removing all cash, not merely the affected portion—still leaves the price below the adjusted buy-below level, so this finding does not change the stated valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Obtain cash by jurisdiction, legal restrictions, repatriation-tax estimates and minimum operating-liquidity requirements, then replace the bridge amount with verified excess cash.

audit_findings.title: Further restructuring costs may have been treated as nonrecurring
audit_findings.magnitude: $93.1 million of FY2025 restructuring costs, equal to 23.4% of the anchor, plus $17 million incurred in the first half of FY2026; remaining costs unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Adding back restructuring charges raises anchor OE, while omitting continuing implementation cash costs raises forecast OE and its capitalized value.
audit_findings.evidence: We expect to incur additional costs in 2026, however the additional costs cannot be quantified at this time.
audit_findings.explanation: Future and recurring-program costs are demonstrated, but the supplied record does not show whether the $398.7 million anchor added back the $93.1 million or whether OE already retains these cash charges. Materiality therefore cannot be established without the anchor reconciliation.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile every restructuring, severance, accelerated-depreciation and disposal adjustment in the anchor; retain recurring cash costs and rerun the valuation if any portion was added back without evidence that spending ceased.

audit_findings.title: Unfunded employee-benefit claims are absent from the bridge
audit_findings.magnitude: $46.4 million total filed deficit, comprising $6.3 million for pension plans, $37.6 million for SERP plans and $2.5 million for postretirement plans; $0.96 per share and 0.7% of base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: Any obligation not already captured through OE should be deducted once in the equity bridge or reflected through future benefit payments in OE.
audit_findings.evidence: As of February 1, 2026 and February 2, 2025, all of the Company’s SERP Plans had projected benefit obligations and accumulated benefit obligations in excess of plan assets as the plans are unfunded.
audit_findings.explanation: The liabilities are demonstrated, but their maximum direct bridge scale is small: a full $46.4 million deduction would reduce the 30%-MOS buy-below level by approximately $0.67 per share. It cannot change the conclusion, and a full deduction could double count amounts already recognized through pension expense or benefit payments.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile actual benefit payments and pension expense included in OE, then deduct only the residual unfunded obligation not already captured, avoiding double counting.
